newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Marzotto shares open steady, HPI down.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Marzotto shares open steady, HPI down.

text.p: Shares in Italian clothing firm Marzotto opened fairly steady in Milan on Monday while stocks in HPI dropped four percent on news that a planned merger between the two had been shelved.
Marzotto opened at 12400 lire, down 0.06 percent, while shares in HPI, which was formed earlier this year, fell to a historic low of 887.0 lire, down 4.43 percent.
Mediobanca, the merchant bank which had arranged the planned merger, fell 3.16 percent to 10290 lire.
The link-up between Marzotto and Holding Partecipazioni Industriale (HPI), which was created earlier this year from parts of financial holding Gemina, collapsed at the weekend.
The deal would have spawned a group worth around 8.24 trillion lire uniting production of a host of top names like German menswear label Hugo Boss, Giorgio Armani and sportswear maker Fila.

Car maker Fiat and Mediobanca were to have held big stakes and Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti's son Maurizio was to have been managing director of the new group, dubbed "big GIM", for Gruppo Industriale Marzotto.
In a joint statement with HPI, Marzotto cited "irreconcilable organisational and financial differences" as reason for the breakdown.
